title: Print Heading Color Hierarchy Shift
description: The styling of the print headings misses a hierarchy step: in classes without \chapter (type=paper, e.g. zwischenbericht) the sequence renders as orange filled -> teal filled -> teal outline -> pink filled -> pink outline, skipping the orange outline. The heading styles must be assigned by effective depth in the class's actual heading sequence so it always reads: orange filled, orange outline, teal filled, teal outline, pink filled, pink outline, etc.
summary:
Heading chip styles are no longer hard-coded per level name; every chip — numbered levels and nested paragraphs alike — is handed a rung on one shared ladder.

print/tex/semio-window.sty, Headings region: \semio@heading@ladder@color / \semio@heading@ladder@style / \semio@heading@ladder@step / \semio@heading@ladder@install replace the 21 fixed \def lines at the top of \semio@heading@installall. Each brand colour holds two consecutive rungs, filled then outlined: orange filled, orange outline, teal filled, teal outline, pink filled, pink outline, then the neutral tail (chrome-panel filled, border-emphasized outline, border-normal outline) for depths past the last hue. \semio@heading@ladder@step also records \semio@heading@rung@<level>.

Bug 1 — rungs were pinned to level names, so an article-style class (type=paper: zwischenbericht, kompaktbericht, paper) has no \chapter and never used the orange-outline rung; \section jumped straight to teal filled. \semio@heading@ladder@install now walks part -> [chapter if the class has one] -> section -> subsection -> subsubsection -> paragraph -> subparagraph, one rung per present level.

Bug 2 — the SemioNest chips ran on a separate two-tone ladder (border-emphasized, then border-normal), so a document nesting under \subsubsection (the mit-bestand zwischenbericht) skipped the pink pair entirely. \semio@nest@style@resolve now computes rung = rung of the level whose number the chip extends (paragraph once c@paragraph > 0, subsubsection otherwise — the same test \semio@nest@build@number makes) + nest depth, and \semio@nest@paragraph dispatches solid vs outline off the ladder style. \semio@nest@style@apply is gone. New \semio@heading@pair@num is the solid counterpart to \semio@heading@pair@nofill@num (explicit number, same argument order) so the nest can pick a renderer by style alone.

Result: report/forschungsbericht (scrreprt) are unchanged; paper-family documents shift down one rung and now read orange filled -> orange outline -> teal filled -> teal outline -> pink filled -> pink outline.

Verified by rebuilding all six print templates light+dark and the mit-bestand zwischenbericht (all exit 0) and rasterizing. A ladder-probe.tex compiled directly with the repo's cached tectonic puts all nine rungs on one page in order (rungs 4-8 are SemioNest depths 1-5) — no shipped document nests deeper than depth 2, so nothing else exercises the tail. mit-bestand p9 light+dark: \section orange outline, \subsection teal filled, \subsubsection teal outline, nest depth 1 pink filled, nest depth 2 pink outline. Report template unchanged in both themes. Rung table, commands and evidence list in the ticket's verification.txt.

Note: `nx run print:test` still aborts on the pre-existing assertion at print/script.ts:689 (\semio_window_vskip_stroke_hairline expecting -3\semio@stroke@hairline) — that section is unchanged from HEAD and unrelated; the suite has no heading assertions.
